"It was such a difficult game, obviously after the international break it's never easy, especially after a defeat in our last game," Calafiori said. "I think we had some tough moments, but I think we deserved the winner. We acted well after the goal we conceded." Leeds are fifth on nine points. UNLIKELY HERO At Stamford Bridge, Henderson was Chelsea's unlikely hero, opening the scoring in the second minute when Cole Palmer, fresh from signing a new contract, drove forward from the halfway line before setting him up to score. Chelsea struck again a minute later when Henderson found Morgan Rogers, whose curling effort deflected in off defender Antonio Silva. Chelsea extended their lead 40 seconds after halftime through Joao Pedro before Evanilson pulled one back for the visitors five minutes later. Joao Pedro netted the Blues' fourth before Henderson capped the win with a superb curling free kick. Henderson, 36, became the oldest player to be directly involved in three-plus Premier League goals since Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2022. Brighton's Maxim de Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam scored in the second half for their side, whose victory came despite seeing Pascal Struijk red-carded in the 57th minute. Brentford's Kristoffer Ajer struck in the 79th to salvage a draw at Villa that left his team fourth on 10 points. Yehor Yarmolyuk had opened the scoring for the visitors before Nicolas Jackson and John McGinn replied for Villa. Ipswich captain Dara O'Shea scored in the 92nd minute to snatch victory over Fulham, who led through Ryan Sessegnon until the 88th minute when Abdoul Ouattara fired in a fine equaliser.

item.title: Spanish lawyer Gonzalez Durantez launches centrist party for November election
item.description: Lawyer Miriam Gonzalez Durantez launched a new Spanish political party on Saturday to run in an early general election on November 29, promising to rise above a growing ideological divide, recover democratic values and depoliticise institutions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lawyer Miriam Gonzalez Durantez launched a new Spanish political party on Saturday to run in an [USN:L1N45V07B TEXT:"early general election"] on November 29, promising to rise above a growing ideological divide, recover democratic values and depoliticise institutions. Gonzalez Durantez, who is married to former British Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg and specialises in international and EU trade law, said the party, called Democracy21, will run in the election in Madrid and Barcelona. The party enters a volatile political landscape after Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called the snap election on Monday following parliament's rejection of measures to address a [USN:L8N45Q06Q TEXT:"mounting housing crisis"]. Opinion polls point to the conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox likely winning a combined parliamentary majority. Referring to the left-right political divide in Spain exemplified by the deep rivalry between the Socialists and the PP, she criticised "two rigid blocs with nothing to foster consensus". Gonzalez Durantez called on Spaniards to "set aside our ideological differences, to stand united, and to work together to safeguard democracy and modernise the country." The crisis has triggered continuing mass protests over home shortages and surging rents, stoked by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman, whose death on Tuesday further angered protesters. Gonzalez Durantez blamed both the ruling coalition and the opposition, which controls most of Spain's regions, for the housing crisis, calling their politicians "a cost, a burden for the country" who expressly failed to develop and urbanise the land. "They haven't used the permits to build housing; instead, they've used them to line the coffers of their city councils. They've imposed so many regulations, many of them absurd, that they've doubled the price per square meter of construction and have made it almost impossible for us to build affordable housing," she told supporters. Central government can set housing legislation and devise nationwide plans for incentives and subsidies, but their implementation, and wider urban planning, is largely devolved to regional governments and municipalities. She said she would identify a problem and not play politics with it. "I won’t use it to pit one group against another, no, I’ll simply fix it."

item.title: Home favourite Zheng sets up China Open final against Andreeva
item.description: French Open winner Mirra Andreeva will face Olympic champion and home favourite Zheng Qinwen in the China Open final after the Russian fourth seed eased past Nikola Bartunkova and unseeded Zheng overpowered Elise Mertens in Saturday's semi-finals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: French Open winner Mirra Andreeva will face Olympic champion and home favourite Zheng Qinwen in the China Open final after the Russian fourth seed eased past Nikola Bartunkova and unseeded Zheng overpowered Elise Mertens in Saturday's semi-finals. Zheng, who received a wildcard entry to the tournament after recovering from an elbow injury, became the first Chinese player to reach the final in Beijing as she outplayed Belgian 13th seed Mertens 7-5 6-2 after Andreeva crushed Bartunkova 6-2 6-2. Zheng made an early break to build a 4-2 lead, but made a number of errors to hand Mertens the break back. But the 24-year-old, who is chasing her first WTA 1000 title on home soil, remained calm to build a 6-5 lead, before her strong crosscourt forehand earned her another break point which she converted when Mertens netted. Zheng dominated the second set to secure her second clash with Andreeva, having beaten the Russian when they met in the 2024 Beijing quarter-finals. "I always want to give my best here. It's like the fifth Grand Slam for me," said Zheng, who reached the semi-final in 2024. In the first semi-final, Andreeva took an hour and 14 minutes to beat Bartunkova and reach her second WTA 1000 final of the year. Czech Bartunkova committed 20 unforced errors, twice as many as Andreeva, as the world number five hit 27 winners to clinch victory. Andreeva is relishing her first China Open final. "Of course, we all know that (Zheng) is playing at home. That's okay. Also, she's been coming back, she's been playing better, she's been beating a lot of great players," the 19-year-old told reporters.

item.title: Neither Putin nor Trump wanted to hang up first, Kremlin aide says after 'very friendly' call
item.description: A conversation on Friday between President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump was "very substantive and friendly" and neither leader wanted to be the first to end the call, Russian news agency Interfax quoted a Kremlin aide as saying.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A conversation on Friday between President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump was "very substantive and friendly" and neither leader wanted to be the first to end the call, Russian news agency Interfax quoted a Kremlin aide as saying. During the call, the presidents agreed that Russia would [USN:FWN45V0WZ TEXT:"supply diesel"] to the US and global markets to lower fuel prices, prompting an unexpected temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian fuel that has [USN:L1N45V0WX TEXT:"dismayed"] Ukraine. The Kremlin said most of the conversation focused on efforts to resolve the war in Ukraine . Putin also [USN:L1N45V0ZL TEXT:"downplayed"] the likelihood of three-way peace talks resuming soon. Interfax cited Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov on Saturday as saying the conversation lasted an hour and a half. "Neither wanted to be the first to hang up," he said. "They hung up simultaneously, literally at the same time." Kyiv is relying on US support in negotiations to end the war. After news of the call broke on Friday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy [USN:L1N45V0WX TEXT:"condemned"] the diesel deal in unusually blunt terms, calling it a "weak decision" and "an investment in a war that must be ended." The West imposed sanctions, including restrictions on Russian energy imports, after Moscow launched the full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022. Efforts to end the fighting have so far stalled, partly over Russia’s demand for four Ukrainian regions it does not fully control. On Friday, negotiators from the US, Ukraine and European countries [USN:L1N45V11A TEXT:"held talks"] in Miami aimed at reaching agreement on a unified peace proposal in the coming weeks that could be presented to Russia, according to a person familiar with the discussions.

item.title: Palmer firma un contrato con el Chelsea hasta 2034
item.description: El centrocampista ofensivo del Chelsea, Cole Palmer, firmó una ampliación de contrato que le mantendrá en Stamford Bridge hasta 2034, anuncio el sábado el club de la Premier League.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El centrocampista ofensivo del Chelsea, Cole Palmer, firmó una ampliación de contrato que le mantendrá en Stamford Bridge hasta 2034, anuncio el sábado el club de la Premier League. El internacional inglés, de 24 años, se ha convertido en una figura clave desde que llegó al Chelsea procedente del Manchester City en 2023, con un registro de 91 goles en 138 partidos en todas las competiciones. Formó parte de la plantilla que ganó el Mundial de Clubes y la UEFA Conference League. "Hablé con los propietarios, con los directores deportivos y, por supuesto, con el entrenador, y me transmitieron mucha confianza, así que lo lógico era firmar", dijo Palmer. "Al hablar también con los jugadores, veo que todos comparten las mismas ambiciones. Tengo la sensación de que aquí ganaremos grandes títulos constantemente". El Chelsea ha acordado contratos a largo plazo con varios jugadores del primer equipo y con jóvenes promesas. El delantero João Pedro firmó recientemente un contrato hasta 2034, y el extremo Pedro Neto acordó el mes pasado un contrato de seis años.

item.title: La presidencia irlandesa de la UE quiere un recorte del 8% al proyecto de presupuesto para 2028-2034
item.description: La presidencia irlandesa de la Unión Europea (UE) propuso el sábado un recorte del 8% al proyecto de presupuesto de la Comisión Europea para el periodo 2028-2034, a 1,6 billones de euros (1,79 billones de dólares), lo que ha suscitado críticas por parte de los Estados miembros más austeros, que consideran que la reducción no es suficiente.
item.dc:creator: Jan Strupczewski, Yun Chee Foo
item.content:encoded: La presidencia irlandesa de la Unión Europea (UE) propuso el sábado un recorte del 8% al proyecto de presupuesto de la Comisión Europea para el periodo 2028-2034, a 1,6 billones de euros (1,79 billones de dólares), lo que ha suscitado críticas por parte de los Estados miembros más austeros, que consideran que la reducción no es suficiente. La propuesta irlandesa supone, a pesar de todo, un aumento del 30% respecto del presupuesto actual del bloque, que abarca el periodo de 2021 a 2027. El presupuesto de la UE es la principal fuente de financiación de todas las políticas fundamentales del bloque de 27 países. La Comisión, el órgano ejecutivo de la UE, ha señalado que el bloque debe destinar más fondos a la defensa y al impulso de la competitividad europea, mientras que algunos Estados miembros desean mantener la mayor parte del gasto destinado al apoyo a la agricultura y al desarrollo regional. "La 'caja de negociación' supone un ahorro del 8%, es decir, 141.000 millones de euros, respecto a la propuesta original de la Comisión", dijo Irlanda, que actualmente y por seis meses preside la UE, refiriéndose a su propuesta de compromiso. Irlanda ajustó la cifra original de la Comisión, de 2 billones de euros, teniendo en cuenta la inflación en siete años, situándola en 1,76 billones de euros a precios de 2025, lo que supuso una reducción del 8%. "Tal y como lo vemos, el marco de negociación sirve para salvar las numerosas diferencias entre los Estados miembros", dijo el ministro irlandés Thomas Byrne en una rueda de prensa. "Nos acerca a la resolución del trilema presupuestario, abordando las conversaciones sobre la mejor forma de financiar nuevas prioridades en materia de competitividad, investigación, innovación, seguridad y defensa, al tiempo que se abordan las políticas fundamentales", añadió. La propuesta establece un recorte del 3% del gasto en desarrollo regional, agricultura y pesca respecto de las propias cifras de la Comisión —la partida más importante del presupuesto— y una reducción del 13% en el gasto en competitividad y seguridad. Los líderes de la UE debatirán la propuesta irlandesa en Bruselas el 15 y 16 de octubre. El presupuesto de la UE, conocido como Marco Financiero Plurianual, debe ser aprobado por los 27 Estados miembros. (1 dólar = 0,8928 euros)

item.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
item.description: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections due next month until September 11, 2027, and called a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the delay.
item.dc:creator: Ali Sawafta, Nidal Al-Mughrabi, Eman Abouhassira
item.content:encoded: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday postponed legislative elections due next month until September 11, 2027, and called a presidential poll for the same date, blaming Israel and the security situation in the Palestinian territories for the delay. Abbas' decree cited "obstacles posed by Israeli measures" and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions for "free, fair and inclusive elections", the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported. In a post on X, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, pointing to the last Palestinian election having been held two decades ago, rejected Abbas' remarks as "yet another ridiculous lie designed to evade responsibility and accountability." There had been serious doubts that the [USN:L8N45G1M5 TEXT:"Palestinian Authority vote"] would go ahead next month. The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-2006, after which Abbas' rival, the Islamist group Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists. Abbas has governed by decree since his presidential mandate expired in 2009. The Palestinian Authority held municipal elections in April in the West Bank and in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, the only city in the enclave to participate. The vote was the first election held in Gaza since 2006. The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel's continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created challenges to preparing for and holding elections this November. In Gaza , the decree pointed to "exceptional security and humanitarian conditions", the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police. The decree called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza to vote. Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said. Israel typically bans the Palestinian Authority from holding elections in East Jerusalem, territory it captured in the 1967 war and later annexed in a move most countries do not recognize. The decision to postpone followed consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address challenges facing the electoral process. PLEDGE TO HOLD VOTE AFTER TWO DECADES Two Palestinian officials told Reuters on Thursday that leaders of Abbas' Fatah movement and rival Hamas had agreed at a meeting in Cairo on Wednesday to postpone the elections. An August poll by the West Bank-based Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research (PSR) showed declining support for both Hamas and Fatah, which many Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank blame for their continuing political divisions. The delay comes just weeks after Abbas reaffirmed the November election timetable in his September 24 address to the UN General Assembly, as he sought to advance internationally backed reforms. Abbas had committed in writing to French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to hold presidential and legislative elections as part of France's recognition of a Palestinian state in September 2025. France's foreign ministry [USN:L1N45V090 TEXT:"said on Thursday"] that holding the elections was essential, and it welcomed the launch of an EU election observation mission.

item.title: Report à 2027 des élections palestiniennes
item.description: Le président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas a annulé samedi les élections législatives prévues en novembre en raison de la dégradation de la situation dans les territoires palestiniens et fixé au 11 septembre 2027 la tenue simultanée des élections présidentielle et législatives, a rapporté l'agence de presse officielle palestinienne WAFA.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas a annulé samedi les élections législatives prévues en novembre en raison de la dégradation de la situation dans les territoires palestiniens et fixé au 11 septembre 2027 la tenue simultanée des élections présidentielle et législatives, a rapporté l'agence de presse officielle palestinienne WAFA. Le décret de Mahmoud Abbas évoque les "obstacles créés par les mesures israéliennes" à la tenue des élections en novembre ainsi que la nécessité de réunir des conditions politiques, sécuritaires et de terrain adaptées à l'organisation d'"élections libres, équitables et inclusives". Il appelle les Palestiniens de Jérusalem, de Cisjordanie et de Gaza à participer au scrutin. De sérieux doutes existaient quant à la tenue du scrutin de l'Autorité palestinienne à la fin novembre. Les Palestiniens n'ont plus organisé d'élections législatives ni présidentielle depuis 2005-2006, à l'issue desquelles le Hamas, rival islamiste du président palestinien Mahmoud Abbas, a pris le contrôle de Gaza en évinçant ses partisans. Le décret précise que les attaques militaires israéliennes, l'expansion des colonies, les violences de colons et les restrictions de circulation en Cisjordanie, y compris à Jérusalem-Est, ainsi que la poursuite du gel par Israël des recettes fiscales palestiniennes, ont créé des difficultés pour préparer et organiser les élections à la date initialement prévue. À Gaza, le décret fait état de "conditions sécuritaires et humanitaires exceptionnelles", du retrait inachevé des forces israéliennes, de l'absence de progrès dans la reconstruction et de la non-mise en oeuvre des dispositions relatives au déploiement de forces internationales de stabilisation et de police. Les restrictions imposées par Israël à l'accès de Gaza et de Jérusalem-Est pour les personnels de la commission électorale et les observateurs internationaux ont également compliqué les préparatifs, ajoute le décret. La décision de report fait suite à une résolution du comité exécutif de l'Organisation de libération de la Palestine (OLP) et à des consultations avec les factions palestiniennes et les forces politiques. Elle vise également à laisser le temps nécessaire à un dialogue national palestinien global afin de renforcer l'unité et de répondre aux défis auxquels est confronté le processus électoral.

item.title: Eritrea asks UN to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia
item.description: Eritrea asked the UN Security Council on Saturday to take deterrent measures against Ethiopia, according to a letter seen by Reuters, saying Addis Ababa's accusations of an invasion by Eritrean forces amounted to a "declaration of war".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Eritrea asked the UN Security Council on Saturday to take deterrent measures against Ethiopia, according to a letter seen by Reuters, saying Addis Ababa's accusations of an invasion by Eritrean forces amounted to a "declaration of war". The [USN:L6N45T121 TEXT:"incursion by Eritrean troops"], which [USN:L8N45Q06L TEXT:"Asmara has denied"] and Reuters could not independently verify, has raised fears of a return to [USN:L6N45M0WY TEXT:"all-out war"] along Ethiopia's northern border where the two Horn of Africa neighbours have clashed before. Conflicts elsewhere in the region and tensions across the Red Sea have further raised the stakes. Eritrean Foreign Minister Osman Saleh said in the letter that the incursion claims were part of an Ethiopian plan to justify a war of aggression. He urged the UN to intervene. "Eritrea requests the UN Security Council to forcefully condemn Ethiopia's deplorable declaration of war against Eritrea ... and take the requisite deterrent measures against it in accordance with Chapter VII of the UN Charter," he wrote. Chapter VII allows for measures ranging from sanctions to military action, though Osman did not specify what measures Eritrea was calling for. Ethiopia itself [USN:L8N45V0CC TEXT:"wrote to Security Council members"] on Friday, stating that Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 km (37 miles) inside the northern region of Tigray in recent days. It warned that the presence of foreign troops left Addis Ababa with no option but to defend itself. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Saturday. ETHIOPIAN TROOPS, MILITIA ALLIES MOVE INTO TIGRAYAN CITY Earlier in the day, Ethiopian government forces and their militia allies entered the Tigrayan city of Adigrat, near the border with Eritrea, three residents said, days after Eritrean troops [USN:L6N45U0QF TEXT:"were "][USN:L6N45U0QF TEXT:"pushed back"] from the strategic city. A video shared on social media and verified by Reuters showed members of a militia allied with the Ethiopian government walking in the streets of Adigrat, which is located 30 km (19 miles) from the border with Eritrea. Three Adigrat residents also told Reuters they had seen the Ethiopian army and an allied militia in the city on Saturday morning, with one of the residents saying they saw soldiers on patrol along with military vehicles. Explosions were reported on Wednesday and Thursday near Adigrat, as the US-based conflict monitor ACLED said Ethiopia used drone strikes against Eritrean forces, who then withdrew from positions near the city. The explosions continued on Friday, according to an Adigrat resident, who told Reuters they had heard repeated explosions overnight and into the morning several kilometres outside town. ETHIOPIAN SEA ACCESS A FLASH POINT Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel said on Friday that Eritrea had shown restraint. He said a 2023 statement by landlocked Ethiopia that it would acquire sovereign access to the sea amounted to declaring a war of aggression against his country. Ethiopia had access to a coastline for decades until Eritrea gained independence from Addis Ababa in 1993. Ethiopia argues that restoring sea access is an existential issue but has said it would be restored through peace and dialogue. Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of backing the rebel alliance that has been battling government troops since September 23 in its northern regions of Tigray, Amhara and Afar. Eritrea has denied doing so. After years of war, Eritrea and Ethiopia made peace in a 2018 agreement that earned Ethiopia's Abiy the Nobel Peace Prize. Eritrea fought in support of Ethiopia’s federal government during a 2020-2022 civil war in Tigray, but relations soured again toward the end of that conflict. The fighting that broke out last month has been the biggest escalation of violence since the Tigray war, in which hundreds of thousands died.

item.title: Ukraine-Une attaque russe fait 20 morts à Zaporijjia, passe d'armes Zelensky-Trump
item.description: Vingt personnes, dont trois enfants, ont été tuées samedi lors d'une attaque russe contre la ville de Zaporijjia, dans le sud de l'Ukraine, au lendemain de l'annonce par le président américain Donald Trump d'un accord levant les sanctions sur le diesel russe, un revers majeur pour Kyiv.
item.dc:creator: Sergiy Chalyi, Max Hunder
item.content:encoded: Vingt personnes, dont trois enfants, ont été tuées samedi lors d'une attaque russe contre la ville de Zaporijjia, dans le sud de l'Ukraine, au lendemain de l'annonce par le président américain Donald Trump d'un accord levant les sanctions sur le diesel russe, un revers majeur pour Kyiv. Une fillette de six ans figure parmi les victimes d'une frappe qui a réduit une partie d'un immeuble résidentiel à l'état de gravats. Dix-huit autres personnes ont été blessées dans cette attaque contre Zaporijjia, ville industrielle dont la périphérie se situe à moins de 30 km de la ligne de front. "Aujourd'hui, la Russie a fêté la levée des sanctions sur les exportations de diesel en larguant cinq bombes planantes sur des immeubles résidentiels à Zaporijjia", a déclaré le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky, dans l'une de ses critiques les plus virulentes à ce jour à l'encontre de la Maison blanche. Donald Trump a rétorqué que Volodimir Zelensky "ferait mieux d'arrêter immédiatement" de bombarder les raffineries russes, ajoutant : "Je suggère qu'ils (les Ukrainiens, NDLR) se trouvent un nouveau dirigeant capable de conclure un accord." L'attaque russe de samedi est la dernière en date d'une série de frappes particulièrement meurtrières en Ukraine ces dernières semaines. Près de 80 civils ont été tués lors de frappes russes mercredi et jeudi, dont au moins 30 dans un bombardement contre la ville-garnison de Kramatorsk, dans l'est du pays, et 22 autres dans une attaque de missile contre la ville de Pryluky, située à environ 130 km à l'est de Kyiv. Le gouverneur local, Mykhaïlo Semikine, a déclaré que la Russie avait frappé plusieurs sites simultanément dans les premières heures de samedi. Des secouristes ont progressé à travers les décombres pour extraire vivants d'autres habitants de l'immeuble. Un homme, dont la jambe était coincée sous les gravats, criait de douleur pendant qu'il était dégagé. "D'AUTRES SIGNAUX SONT NÉCESSAIRES" Zaporijjia, qui comptait plus de 700.000 habitants avant la guerre, est régulièrement visée par les bombardements russes, dont l'intensité s'est accrue au cours des derniers mois. "La nuit dernière a constitué une nouvelle confirmation que la Russie considère tout allègement de la pression comme un signal lui permettant soi-disant de continuer à faire la guerre, de continuer à larguer des bombes sur les villes. D'autres signaux sont nécessaires", a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky. Une attaque de missile menée samedi après-midi a également frappé un restaurant à Kyiv, blessant sept personnes. Des drones russes ont survolé la capitale ukrainienne tout au long de la journée dans le cadre d'une nouvelle vague massive de bombardements, la plus importante depuis les premiers jours de la guerre. Le ministère russe de la Défense a déclaré samedi en début se soirée que ses drones avaient frappé plus tôt un centre de traitement de données à Kyiv ainsi qu'un cargo transportant des fournitures militaires vers le port ukrainien d'Odessa. Dans un communiqué, il a ajouté que le site de Kyiv était utilisé par les forces armées ukrainiennes pour collecter, traiter et stocker des renseignements. Reuters n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier ces informations dans l'immédiat. La décision de Donald Trump de lever les sanctions sur les exportations de diesel russe intervient alors que son administration cherche à enrayer la hausse des prix des carburants, qui ont bondi dans le contexte du conflit opposant les États-Unis à l'Iran. Kyiv avait au contraire exhorté Washington à accroître la pression sur la Russie afin de la contraindre à engager de véritables négociations pour mettre fin à la guerre, qui dure depuis quatre ans et demi. L'ACCORD SUR LE DIESEL A PRIS KYIV PAR SURPRISE Donald Trump a en outre critiqué les frappes ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes, estimant qu'elles avaient contribué à faire grimper les prix mondiaux. Kyiv dit vouloir un arrêt total des attaques visant les infrastructures énergétiques des deux camps, alors que Moscou continue de pilonner le réseau électrique ukrainien. Samedi, plusieurs secteurs de Kyiv et de sa région ont été privés d'électricité, provoquant l'arrêt complet du métro de la capitale pour la deuxième fois de la semaine. Ces dernières frappes sont intervenues après des discussions à Miami entre responsables ukrainiens et européens et négociateurs américains, vendredi, en vue d'élaborer une proposition commune pour mettre fin à la guerre, selon une source proche du dossier. L'agence de presse officielle russe Tass, citant une source, a rapporté samedi que les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner pourraient se rendre à Moscou au cours des deux prochaines semaines. Donald Trump a annoncé l'accord sur le diesel alors que les négociations de vendredi étaient en cours, une décision qui, selon Volodimir Zelensky, a pris Kyiv par surprise. Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a déclaré, à l'issue d'un entretien téléphonique avec son homologue américain, qu'une reprise immédiate des pourparlers de paix était peu probable, invoquant les attaques de drones ukrainiens contre Moscou. Par ailleurs, quatre civils ont été tués et cinq autres blessés à la suite d'attaques ukrainiennes contre la région de Louhansk, sous contrôle russe dans l'est de l'Ukraine, a déclaré samedi le gouverneur local installé par Moscou. Reuters n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier cette information de manière indépendante et l'Ukraine n'a pas fait de commentaire dans l'immédiat.

item.title: Riders stage safety protest before start of Giro di Lombardia
item.description: Riders at the Giro di Lombardia staged a five-minute protest before the start of Saturday's race to highlight growing safety concerns following a series of incidents involving race vehicles, the tournament organisers said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Riders at the Giro di Lombardia staged a five-minute protest before the start of Saturday's race to highlight growing safety concerns following a series of incidents involving race vehicles, the tournament organisers said. The protest came days after riders Thomas Gloag and Marcel Camprubi were struck by a police motorcycle travelling in the opposite direction during Tre Valli Varesine. "At the start of Il Lombardia, the riders came together to send an important message, stopping for five minutes to urge all road users to behave responsibly and show mutual respect, both during races and in everyday life," organisers RCS Sport said in a social media post. After organisers completed the start countdown, the peloton remained stationary, before Belgium's double Olympic champion Remco Evenepoel stepped forward to explain the riders' action. "There’s too many incidents happening with vehicles in the race," Evenepoel said. "Unfortunately we lost the life of a brother and of a colleague of us, so we want to make this statement to show to the world that we cannot keep accepting the fact that guys are getting injured or literally dying in what we like the most to do." Evenepoel was referring to the death of British cyclist Finlay [USN:L4N44B13Q TEXT:"Tarling"], younger brother of Ineos rider Josh Tarling, who was killed in a collision with a vehicle during the Tour of Portugal on August 14. The demonstration delayed the start of the final Monument race of the season by five minutes before the peleton set off. Reuters has contacted the International Cycling Union (UCI) for comment.

item.title: Philips wins Dutch court battle with shareholders over recall
item.description: A Dutch court on Saturday dismissed demands by shareholders of health technology company Philips for an investigation into allegations of misleading disclosures and management failures linked to the company's recall of sleep apnea devices.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Dutch court on Saturday dismissed demands by shareholders of health technology company Philips (PHG.AS) for an investigation into allegations of misleading disclosures and management failures linked to the company's recall of sleep apnea devices. A large group of shareholders had [USN:L5N3VB062 TEXT:"demanded"] a court inquiry, as they said Philips executives had responded too late to the problems that led to the massive recall and had failed to adequately inform investors. Philips' shares lost about two thirds of their value when the company recalled around 15 million sleep apnea devices in 2021, after discovering that the foam in the machines could release harmful substances and might pose health risks. The Enterprise Chamber of the Amsterdam Court of Appeal in its ruling said it had found no indication that Philips had known about the problems long before it issued any warning. It also said there was no reason to assume executives should have intervened earlier at the Respironics subsidiary that made the devices. Philips had denied the accusations made by the shareholders and said it welcomed the court's decision. The sleep apnea devices recall led to probes in multiple countries, including France, where prosecutors are still investigating charges of aggravated fraud and failure to report safety risks. Philips in 2024 agreed to pay $1.1 billion to settle all personal injury claims related to the devices filed in the US.

item.title: La India detiene a cientos e impone un confinamiento en Delhi para impedir protestas
item.description: La policía detuvo el sábado en Delhi a cientos de manifestantes y al fundador del movimiento juvenil "Cucarachas", mientras las fuerzas de seguridad cerraban al tráfico algunas zonas de la capital para impedir una manifestación en la que se exigía la dimisión del presidente de la Comisión Electoral de la India.
item.dc:creator: Saurabh Sharma, Sunil Kataria, Sakshi Dayal
item.content:encoded: La policía detuvo el sábado en Delhi a cientos de manifestantes y al fundador del movimiento juvenil "Cucarachas", mientras las fuerzas de seguridad cerraban al tráfico algunas zonas de la capital para impedir una manifestación en la que se exigía la dimisión del presidente de la Comisión Electoral de la India. Miles de agentes de policía y personal paramilitar se desplegaron por toda la ciudad, se suspendieron los servicios de Internet móvil en el distrito financiero central y se cerraron decenas de estaciones de metro y mercados, mientras las autoridades tomaban medidas para impedir una concentración organizada por el movimiento "Cucarachas". La protesta iba dirigida contra el presidente de la Comisión Electoral, Gyanesh Kumar, por una revisión de las listas electorales que, según los críticos, beneficia de manera desproporcionada al Partido Bharatiya Janata (BJP) del primer ministro Narendra Modi. El movimiento tenía previsto reunir a miles de personas en Jantar Mantar, un lugar designado para las protestas en el centro de Delhi. Sin embargo, las fuerzas de seguridad acordonaron la zona antes de que comenzara la manifestación. No obstante, hubo pequeñas protestas en otros puntos de la ciudad, entre ellos un popular mercado de artesanía y el monumento al líder del movimiento por la libertad Mahatma Gandhi, donde los manifestantes corearon consignas exigiendo la dimisión de Kumar. "¡Viva la revolución!", coreaban algunos jóvenes manifestantes en el centro de Delhi mientras la policía los perseguía y arrastraba a decenas de ellos a los autobuses para llevárselos, pese a que más seguían llegando, según un testigo de Reuters. "Esto supone una violación de los derechos del pueblo y el país ya no lo va a tolerar más", dijo Yogendra Solanki a Reuters mientras la policía se lo llevaba escoltado. La policía también detuvo al fundador del Partido del Pueblo Cucaracha, Abhijeet Dipke, y a Saurav Das y Ashutosh Ranka, otros de sus líderes, cuando su vuelo procedente de Bombay aterrizó en Delhi, informó el grupo en un comunicado. DELHI, EN CONFINAMIENTO PARA IMPEDIR LAS PROTESTAS Las imágenes de televisión mostraban a Dipke desafiando a los agentes que se le acercaban a bordo del avión. "He venido para que me detengan, deténganme (…) No les tengo miedo", dijo. "No, esto no es una detención", respondió uno de los agentes. "Por favor, coopere". El movimiento condenó lo que calificó de "detención autoritaria" de sus líderes, exigió su liberación inmediata y dijo que la protesta continuaría de todos modos. Según mostraron los canales de televisión, también fueron detenidos algunos diputados de la oposición y exministros. La policía no hizo ningún comentario inmediato sobre las detenciones. En toda la extensa capital, con unos 20 millones de habitantes, las fuerzas de seguridad instalaron controles en las principales carreteras y en los puntos de acceso a la ciudad. Agentes de policía subieron a los autobuses en busca de manifestantes, mientras que los vehículos fueron sometidos a inspecciones. Las barricadas y los bloques de hormigón interrumpieron el tráfico, mientras que en las vías principales se apostaron vehículos antidisturbios equipados con lanzadores de gas lacrimógeno. NUEVO RETO PARA MODI Las manifestaciones suponen una de las pruebas más serias hasta la fecha para Modi, a raíz de las acusaciones de que las autoridades electorales revisaron indebidamente los censos electorales antes de las recientes elecciones estatales. Las protestas han cobrado impulso desde la semana pasada, cuando el periódico Indian Express informó de que dos comisionados electorales habían cuestionado y mostrado su desacuerdo con Kumar por las revisiones, que eliminaron aproximadamente 130 millones de nombres de las listas electorales. Kumar no ha hecho declaraciones al respecto, pero la Comisión Electoral y el BJP han negado las acusaciones de irregularidades. El BJP dijo que su éxito electoral refleja la popularidad de Modi y el crecimiento económico de la India, y acusa a los partidos de la oposición de difundir información errónea porque no han logrado ganar las elecciones. No obstante, las protestas casi a diario, suponen un nuevo reto para Modi, apenas unos meses después de que las manifestaciones por las filtraciones de exámenes obligaron a su ministro de Educación a dimitir. Los disturbios se producen además en vísperas de una serie de importantes elecciones estatales que comenzarán a principios de 2027. Las restricciones del sábado demostraron que el Gobierno de Modi ha "declarado oficialmente la guerra a su propio pueblo", dijo K.C. Venugopal, uno de los principales líderes del Partido del Congreso, el principal de la oposición. El portavoz del BJP, Sambit Patra, dijo que la democracia había prevalecido sobre el dominio de las turbas.

item.title: Singapore not ideal for sprints, say Hamilton and Verstappen
item.description: Singapore's Formula One circuit needs re-designing and lacks entertainment value for a sprint race, Saturday's sprint winner Max Verstappen and runner-up Lewis Hamilton said after the 20-lap race involved little overtaking.
item.dc:creator: Tom Westbrook
item.content:encoded: Singapore's Formula One circuit needs re-designing and lacks entertainment value for a sprint race, Saturday's sprint winner Max Verstappen and runner-up Lewis Hamilton said after the 20-lap race involved little overtaking. Rain delayed the start of the inaugural sprint at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, and with overtaking nearly impossible the only drama came in the form of collisions and a record nine retirements. "I think we shouldn't host a sprint where you can't pass," Red Bull's polesitter Verstappen told reporters after notching his [USN:L1N45W02M TEXT:"first victory"] at the circuit. "I'm fine, I just do my thing... but it's not what I like. The overtake mode, it barely does anything here. You don't really gain a lot on the straights ... we need to have a longer straight or like more of a proper hairpin to overtake." Mercedes' George Russell spun into the wall on the final turn of the first lap when he was leading the sprint while the two McLaren cars collided on the last lap while chasing the final podium spot. SAFETY CAR In between, six of the 20 laps ran behind a safety car, which is commonplace in Singapore due to crashes, while 11 of the 16 race wins have come from pole position. "I love the race here, (but) I was just saying to Max, I think they need to change the track to maybe a longer straight somewhere in order to allow it to be truly a great racing circuit," Hamilton said. "It's a great track to drive over a single lap and qualifying, but ... there's like one place, really, that you could potentially get close to overtaking. "I thought it was fun, but if it was dry, that would have been probably the most boring race for you to have watched. It was the rain, that made it exciting." Reduced distance sprint races, with eight points going to the winner, are held on Saturdays with sprint qualifying replacing the usual second Friday practice sessions. Singapore's was the sixth and final sprint race this season and it is not on next year's 10-event sprint calendar, though another city circuit in Monaco is on the schedule -- a venue Ferrari's hometown hero Charles Leclerc said was not ideal. "I don't think it makes sense to have any sprint races on city tracks in general," said Leclerc, who finished third in Singapore's sprint. "Here or Monaco, I don't think it adds anything to the weekend."

item.title: Ducks ride versatile offense into encounter vs. winless Flames
item.description: The Anaheim Ducks arrive in Calgary to face the struggling Flames on Saturday night with a level of confidence beyond having won three of four games to start the season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Anaheim Ducks arrive in Calgary to face the struggling Flames on Saturday night with a level of confidence beyond having won three of four games to start the season. The Ducks are flying high with the knowledge they can pull off a victory without offensive contributions from their biggest guns. Anaheim comes to Calgary after a decisive 5-1 win at the Winnipeg Jets on Friday in a game in which the difference makers were fourth-line players. Judd Caulfield, Tim Washe and Jeff Malott all recorded their first career multi-point game. Caulfield, 25, scored his first NHL goal. "They had a special night," Ducks coach Joel Quenneville said. "They scored a couple off the rush, almost had a third one off the rush, had a couple shifts in the third with good possession and cycle time. We couldn't ask for anything more." Anaheim's Beckett Sennecke notched a pair of assists, giving him six points (three goals, three assists) in a four-game point streak to start the season. Leo Carlsson and Cutter Gauthier, however, were scoreless on Friday. It was a non-issue with the lower-profile players stepping up to hand Winnipeg its first regulation-time loss of the season. "It feels great to get that first one," Caulfield said of his first big-league tally. "It was a great play by Washe to get that puck out of the zone and (Malott) had great speed taking the puck to the net and left it easy for me to score." After Lukas Dostal started in goal in Winnipeg, expect Ville Husso to start at the position for Anaheim on Saturday. The Flames, the only NHL team without a point, are trying to find any spark in the early going. Calgary, which is coming off a 7-3 loss to the Colorado Avalanche on Thursday, has lost all four of its games this season, by a combined score of 23-6. As lopsided as the results have been, including the loss to Colorado, there is a belief that Thursday's game was a step forward for Calgary. "In the first (period), I thought we played with some energy and pace and created a lot of chances," captain Mikael Backlund said. "It's obviously really tough and hard and frustrating to lose again. We've got to learn from it, find a way to play a really solid 60 (minutes). We haven't done that yet, and it's time we do that on Saturday." As much as the Flames are struggling offensively, there is a strong thought that their fortunes will change if they improve defensively. All four losses have been blowouts, and the goaltending duo of Dustin Wolf and Devin Cooley believe they must find a way to make a difference and help their teammates find momentum. "We've given up too many goals; that's the bottom line," Wolf said. "I think sometimes we can laugh about it, but our objective is to get points, and we're not doing a good enough job -- I'm not doing a good enough job -- of helping our team do that." The Pacific Division rivals will meet again Tuesday night in Anaheim, Calif., in the second game of a home-and-home series. --Field Level Media

item.title: Verstappen se lleva su primera victoria de la temporada en una carrera al sprint caótica en Singapur
item.description: Max Verstappen, de Red Bull, saboreó la victoria en Singapur por primera vez en la temporada. El piloto neerlandés, que partió desde la "pole", se impuso en una caótica carrera al sprint, tras un retraso de más de 30 minutos en la salida debido a las fuertes lluvias y en la que nueve autos abandonaron la carrera, lo que supone un récord para este tipo de competencia.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: Max Verstappen, de Red Bull, saboreó la victoria en Singapur por primera vez en la temporada. El piloto neerlandés, que partió desde la "pole", se impuso en una caótica carrera al sprint, tras un retraso de más de 30 minutos en la salida debido a las fuertes lluvias y en la que nueve autos abandonaron la carrera, lo que supone un récord para este tipo de competencia. Verstappen cruzó la línea de meta por delante de Lewis Hamilton y Charles Leclerc, ambos de Ferrari. "Quiero ganar mañana. No considero esto una victoria en el sentido de haber ganado realmente un Gran Premio", dijo Verstappen. El líder del campeonato de Mercedes, Kimi Antonelli, se hizo con el cuarto puesto tras una colisión entre los dos McLaren en la última vuelta, mientras que su compañero de equipo, George Russell, sufrió un accidente cuando iba en cabeza en la primera vuelta. Verstappen había conservado su "pole position" tras librarse de una sanción por adelantar bajo bandera amarilla el viernes, pero el holandés tuvo una salida lenta, mientras que Russell se ponía en cabeza y Hamilton remontaba rápidamente del sexto al tercer puesto. La escapada de Russell terminó en la última curva de la primera vuelta, cuando su neumático trasero se subió al bordillo y derrapó contra el muro, lo que provocó la salida del auto de seguridad. "La salida volvió a ser horrible, así que sin duda es algo en lo que tenemos que mejorar, porque si mañana ocurre algo así, se acaba la carrera a menos que pase alguna locura", añadió Verstappen. "Después de eso, lo único que quieres es mantener la calma y el control, porque sabes que aquí no se puede adelantar". "UN ERROR TONTO" DE RUSSELL Russell explicó que un error de cálculo le hizo derrapar en la última curva. "Al salir de la curva, tenía más consumo de batería del que pensaba. Me empujó un poco más hacia fuera de lo que esperaba y entonces me salí por la línea blanca", explicó Russell. "Sí, un error tonto. Con consecuencias muy, muy graves". La carnicería continuó cuando Lance Stroll y Sergio Pérez se retiraron tras chocar entre sí, y a Isack Hadjar, de Red Bull, se le pidió detener su auto debido a un problema técnico. El vehículo de seguridad permaneció en pista después de que el Alpine de Franco Colapinto también se detuvo, y la carrera no se reanudó hasta la séptima vuelta. Verstappen lideraba por delante de los Ferrari de Hamilton y Leclerc, mientras que los McLaren de Oscar Piastri y Lando Norris se situaban entre los cinco primeros, por delante de Antonelli. Sin embargo, las esperanzas de McLaren de subir al podio se desvanecieron cuando el vigente campeón Norris rozó a Piastri y ambos coches hicieron un trompo, lo que permitió a Antonelli ascender al cuarto puesto y ampliar su ventaja en el campeonato sobre Russell a 89 puntos. "Miré por los retrovisores y vi las luces rojas de la parte trasera de los McLaren. Así que supe que había pasado algo", explicó Leclerc. La sesión de clasificación para la carrera del domingo se retrasó debido a la lluvia.

item.title: Norris apologises after collision dashes McLaren sprint hopes
item.description: World champion Lando Norris apologised to his McLaren team after a final-lap collision with team mate Oscar Piastri wrecked their pursuit of a podium finish at a chaotic Singapore Grand Prix sprint on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: World champion Lando Norris apologised to his McLaren team after a final-lap collision with team mate Oscar Piastri wrecked their pursuit of a podium finish at a [USN:L1N45W02M TEXT:"chaotic Singapore Grand Prix sprint"] on Saturday. The McLaren duo were chasing Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, who was struggling with his tyres in the dying stages of the 20-lap sprint, when disaster struck on the final lap. Norris, running fifth behind Piastri in fourth, attempted to overtake his team mate but clipped the Australian's rear tyre with his front wheel, sending both cars spinning and handing Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli fourth place. "Sorry about that. Obviously I didn't want that to happen but I thought I was fully alongside. I just ran out of space at the apex but I was there," Norris said over the team radio. While Norris limped home to eighth place to claim the final point available, Piastri was forced to retire as he became one of nine cars that did not finish - a record number of retirements for a Formula One sprint race. "I'd rather just go back and review it," Norris told Sky Sports. "I apologised to them that one of the cars is out but, like I said, the rest of it we'll go review." Piastri said he had not seen the incident properly to comment but downplayed its significance as they were not in high points scoring positions. "From where I sit, it's for fourth and fifth for a sprint race, so I'm not that bothered either way," Piastri said. "Just obviously it's a lot of work now for the team to get both cars fixed (ahead of qualifying for Sunday's race). Just a shame for the team." 'SIMPLY NOT ACCEPTABLE' Both McLaren drivers were summoned to meet the stewards after the collision but no further action was taken. The FIA said both drivers "contributed to the incident and that neither driver was wholly or predominantly to blame for the collision." McLaren team principal Andrea Stella was not impressed with his drivers, however, adding that scoring just one point was not enough. "Seeing two McLarens making contact like that is simply not acceptable. This is something that we will discuss with our drivers," he said. "We will do it in private. We will reiterate that the team interest is far bigger than any of us. There's no ego, there's no person that is bigger than the interest of the McLaren Formula One team. "I'm sure, like always, this will be conversations that will lead to the team being more united and even stronger." Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the sprint and the Dutchman, who also [USN:L1N45W02M TEXT:"clinched pole for Sunday's race"] , leapfrogged Norris to climb to fifth in the world championship standings.

item.title: Struggling Blues eager to ignite offense vs. Blue Jackets
item.description: The St. Louis Blues will look to halt a three-game losing streak when they host the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The St. Louis Blues will look to halt a three-game losing streak when they host the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday night. The Blues have hit sour notes following a 4-0 victory over the Dallas Stars in a season opener on Oct. 2. St. Louis fell 3-2 in overtime in its most recent outing, at home against the San Jose Sharks on Thursday. "I think we certainly felt like we gave ourselves an opportunity to win the game, so only coming away with one point is disappointing," Blues defenseman Cam Fowler said. "But there's a lot that we can build off of as well ... some points in our game that we can work on moving forward and getting ready for Saturday." St. Louis has just five goals during its winless stretch (0-2-1). Blues coach Jim Montgomery vented his frustration over the team's lack of goal scoring with a colorful quote following Thursday's loss. "Right now, if we fell out of a boat and we were trying to score a goal, we would not hit the ocean, and it's causing problems," he said. Connor McMichael and Dillon Dube each scored a goal for the Blues on Thursday. Off-season additions McMichael (two goals, two assists) and Mason McTavish (two goals, one assist) are leading the way offensively for the Blues, while captain Robert Thomas has failed to record a point through the first four games. Thomas has topped the Blues in points over each of the past two seasons and has 373 points in 361 games over his previous five seasons. The Blue Jackets should be feeling good heading into Saturday's game after outlasting the Pittsburgh Penguins 3-2 in a shootout on Friday. Kent Johnson scored the lone shootout goal to secure the victory. Damon Severson and Mathieu Olivier also found the back of the net in regulation for Columbus. The Blue Jackets controlled the majority of the play against the Penguins, outshooting them 45-22. "You saw a lot tonight how we wanna play; Columbus Blue Jacket hockey was out there tonight for the most part," Columbus coach Rick Bowness said. "We dominated the game at certain times, and yeah they had some flashes, they're an excellent hockey team over there. For the most part that's Columbus Blue Jackets hockey, we're going north, we're hard to play against. That was good to see." Severson, who was playing in his first game this season, also picked up an assist, and Cole Sillinger set up two goals in the win. Cam Talbot made 20 saves and denied all three attempts in the shootout en route to his first win in a Blue Jackets uniform. Talbot signed with the team as a free agent on a one-year, $950,000 deal last month. Columbus will play on the road for the first time this season on Saturday. The Blue Jackets have dominated the Blues in recent seasons, winning the previous six meetings. --Field Level Media

item.title: Major Saudi conferences to proceed, organisers say, despite deadly airport attack
item.description: The organisers of two major Saudi energy and investment conferences said their events will go ahead this month and reassured visitors on security, after missile attacks on Riyadh's airport left four people dead and an airliner heavily damaged this week.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: The organisers of two major Saudi energy and investment conferences said their events will go ahead this month and reassured visitors on security, after [USN:L1N45V07H TEXT:"missile attacks"] on Riyadh's airport left four people dead and an airliner heavily damaged this week. The attacks led to widespread flight disruptions, with people taking land routes or circuitous alternative flights. The UK, France and Germany have warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh. Riyadh is sticking to plans to convene global events and trying to draw in investment even amid escalating war with the Iran-backed Houthis in neighbouring Yemen that has seen the kingdom attacked dozens of times over the past weeks. Organisers of the World Petroleum Congress, set to host top global oil executives and policymakers from Sunday to Thursday, said it would proceed as planned with foreign leaders and ministers in attendance, an email sent to delegates said. "Your comfort is our priority," it said, noting that alternative routes to Riyadh, including via a four-hour drive from Dammam on the kingdom's eastern coast, were available. Italian Energy Minister Gilberto Pichetto Fratin on Friday said he would not fly to Riyadh for the International Energy Forum Ministerial Meeting, an event on WPC's sidelines, but would participate via video link. The Future Investment Initiative, launched by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman as the kingdom's flagship investment conference a decade ago, would also proceed as planned from October 26-29, organisers said. "Safety and well-being remain our highest priority," a statement attributed to FII CEO Maha Al Saud said. "Comprehensive security measures will be in place at Riyadh's airports, our conference venues and official hotels, with coordinated arrangements for participants' transportation," it said. Chief executives of some of the world's biggest financial institutions such as JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon and Citi's Jane Fraser were on the list of expected attendees. Citi and JPMorgan did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Houthis have said airliners should avoid Saudi airspace, declaring it a zone of military operations after the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an offensive against the group earlier this month. Germany's Lufthansa has suspended Riyadh flights through October 16 while Gulf carriers Etihad Airways and Flydubai have cancelled flights to and from the Saudi capital scheduled for October 10. Saudi Arabia has responded to Houthi attacks with a wave of strikes on missile launcher sites, vowing to protect the kingdom, and says it has intercepted many ballistic missiles fired by the group.

item.title: China proposes stricter car design, testing rules, including ban on fully hidden door handles
item.description: China's industry ministry on Saturday proposed tighter oversight of automakers' innovative designs and research and development testing. It said some manufacturers had rushed out new models without enough validation, which raised safety and environmental risks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's industry ministry on Saturday proposed tighter oversight of automakers' innovative designs and research and development testing. It said some manufacturers had rushed out new models without enough validation, which raised safety and environmental risks. • From January 1, 2027, automakers seeking approval for new models must submit more technical details on innovative designs and testing. Models that are poorly tested or backed by false data will be rejected, the draft said • Models that already have approval must file information on their innovative designs by July 1, 2027. If they do not and have safety hazards, automakers must halt production and recall them • The draft bans fully hidden door handles and foldable or flexible displays. It also bars use of "zero-gravity" or swivel seats while driving • Key functions such as lights and wipers must keep physical controls • The ministry drafted the rules with three other agencies and is taking public comment until November 10

item.title: EU's Irish presidency wants 8% cut to proposed 2028-2034 budget plan
item.description: The Irish EU presidency proposed on Saturday an 8% cut in the European Commission's budget plan for the period 2028 to 2034 to €1.6 trillion ($1.79 trillion), drawing criticism from more frugal member states that the reduction is not deep enough.
item.dc:creator: Jan Strupczewski, Yun Chee Foo
item.content:encoded: The Irish EU presidency proposed on Saturday an 8% cut in the European Commission's budget plan for the period 2028 to 2034 to €1.6 trillion ($1.79 trillion), drawing criticism from more frugal member states that the reduction is not deep enough. The Irish proposal still marks a 30% increase over the bloc's current budget, which runs from 2021 to 2027. The EU budget is the main source of financing for all of the 27-country bloc's main policies. The Commission, the EU executive, has said the bloc needs to spend more on defence and boosting European competitiveness, while some member states want to retain most of the expenditure to support farming and regional development. "The Negotiating Box provides savings of 8%, or €141 billion, on the Commission's original proposal," said Ireland, current holder of the EU's six-month rotating presidency, referring to its compromise proposal. Ireland put the Commission's original €2 trillion figure adjusted for inflation over the seven-year period at €1.76 trillion based on 2025 prices, which resulted in an 8% reduction. IRELAND SAYS PLAN SEEKS TO RECONCILE COMPETING DEMANDS "As we see it, the negotiating box acts to bridge the many differences between the member states," Irish minister Thomas Byrne told a press conference. "It brings us closer to resolving the budgetary trilemma, addressing the talks of how best to finance new priorities in competitiveness, research, innovation, security and defence while at the same time addressing core policies," he said. The proposal sets out a 3% cut in spending on regional development, agriculture and fisheries from the Commission's own figures — the biggest outlay in the budget — and a 13% reduction in spending on competitiveness and security. It foresees €55 billion in new financing options derived from customs duties, a share of the cash EU governments get from selling CO2 emissions permits to companies and an annual lump-sum contribution from large companies operating in the EU, among other sources. Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz joined ministers from Sweden and the Netherlands - all three countries are net contributors to the budget - in criticising the Irish proposal. "The EU budget must be affordable for those who bear the main burden of financing it," he said. However, lawmakers in the European Parliament, which wants a 10% increase in the Commission's €2 trillion proposal, said the Irish plan would weaken Europe and would not win their consent. EU leaders will discuss the Irish proposal in Brussels on October 15 to 16. The EU budget, which is known as the [USN:L8N41B114 TEXT:"Multiannual Financial Framework"], needs to be agreed by all 27 member states. ($1 = 0.8928 euros)

item.title: Israeli strikes kill five people in Gaza, medics say
item.description: Israeli strikes killed at least five Palestinians in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on Saturday, health officials said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israeli strikes killed at least five Palestinians in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on Saturday, health officials said. Medics said an Israeli strike killed four people near Panda Mall in Gaza City, while another killed one person in the Tuffah neighbourhood further south of the city. The Israeli military said the two strikes targeted militants, without giving further information. Israel has stepped up strikes against Hamas in recent weeks, saying the Palestinian militant group has been rearming and carrying out attacks in violation of the ceasefire. Hamas denies rebuilding its arsenal or planning attacks and accuses Israel of undermining a US-brokered ceasefire agreed a year ago. The ceasefire calls for eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made towards implementing a deal to end the conflict that includes terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops. Gaza health officials have said at least 1,400 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since the truce was agreed last October. Israel says four of its soldiers have been killed by militants in Gaza over the same period. The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led [USN:L1N45T04T TEXT:"October 7, 2023 attacks"] on Israel, which killed 1,200 people, while a further 251 were taken hostage. Israel's subsequent bombardment and ground operations in Gaza have killed more than 74,000 people, according to Gaza health officials.

item.title: Germany sticks to Russia sanctions after Trump announcement on diesel
item.description: Germany said on Saturday it would maintain sanctions against Russia over its war on Ukraine following US President Donald Trump's announcement that his administration had temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany said on Saturday it would maintain sanctions against Russia over its war on Ukraine following US President Donald Trump's announcement that his administration had temporarily [USN:L1N45V0MW TEXT:"lifted US sanctions"] on Russian fuel. "The federal government has taken note of the US decision relating to Russian diesel deliveries," government spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said in a statement. He said Germany's position remained clear: "The federal government remains committed to the decisions on sanctions against Russia and is working with its European partners on further sanctions." He said Germany's support for Ukraine was unchanged and diplomatic efforts to reach a solution would continue. Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices. He said his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its war on Ukraine. Prices for diesel, used for agriculture, heating homes and trucking, have risen to near record levels, posing a risk for Trump's fellow Republicans ahead of the November 3 congressional elections that will determine whether they maintain thin control of Congress. Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who visited Kyiv last weekend, has said repeatedly that Germany, Ukraine's largest European donor, would not reduce its support for the Kyiv government.

item.title: Palmer signs Chelsea contract until 2034
item.description: The England international has become a key figure since joining Chelsea from Manchester City.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chelsea attacking midfielder Cole Palmer has signed a contract extension to keep him at Stamford Bridge until 2034, the Premier League club said on Saturday. The 24-year-old England international has become a key figure since joining Chelsea from Manchester City in 2023, scoring 91 goals in 138 appearances across all competitions. He was part of the squad that won the Club World Cup and UEFA Conference League. "Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and obviously the manager, they gave me a lot of confidence so it was only right to sign," Palmer said. "Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions. I feel like we win major trophies here consistently." Chelsea have agreed long-term contracts Chelsea with several first-team players and emerging talent. Forward [USN:L6N44J020 TEXT:"Joao Pedro"] recently signed a deal through 2034, and winger Pedro Neto agreed a six-year contract last month. Chelsea, 10th in the Premier League table, host Bournemouth on Saturday.

item.title: Verstappen claims first Singapore win as nine retirements mar chaotic sprint
item.description: The victory was the first of any kind for the Dutchman in Singapore as he took the chequered flag ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: Red Bull's Max Verstappen tasted victory in Singapore for the first time as the polesitter won a chaotic sprint on Saturday after the [USN:L1N45W02H TEXT:"start was delayed by over 30 minutes"] due to heavy rain while nine cars retired, a record for sprint races. The victory was the first of any kind for the Dutchman in Singapore as he took the chequered flag ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc. "I want to win tomorrow. I don't see this as a win in terms of actually winning a Grand Prix," Verstappen said. Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli was gifted fourth place after the two McLarens collided on the final lap while his team mate George Russell crashed out of the lead on lap one. Verstappen had kept his [USN:L1N45V0HG TEXT:"pole position"] after escaping a penalty for overtaking under a yellow flag on Friday but the Dutchman made a slow start as Russell stormed ahead and Hamilton swiftly moved up from sixth to third. Russell's sprint ended on the last turn of lap one when his rear tyre went over the kerb and he spun into the wall to bring the safety car out. "The start was horrendous again, so that's definitely something that we need to improve on because if you have something like that tomorrow, that's your race over if nothing crazy happens," Verstappen added. "After that, you just want to keep it calm and under control because you know that you can't pass around here." 'SILLY MISTAKE' FOR RUSSELL Russell said a miscalculation caused him to spin out at the last corner. "I came through the corner, had more battery deployment than I thought. Pushed me a little bit wider than I hoped and then I just went on the white line," Russell said. "Yeah, silly mistake. Big, big consequences." The carnage continued when Lance Stroll and Sergio Perez retired after they collided and Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was asked to stop his car due to a technical issue. The safety car remained on track after Franco Colapinto's Alpine also came to a standstill and they did not resume racing until lap seven. Verstappen led from the Ferraris of Hamilton and Leclerc while the McLarens of Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris were in the top five ahead of Antonelli. MCLARENS COLLIDE ON FINAL LAP McLaren's hopes of a podium vanished, however, when reigning champion Norris nudged into Piastri and the two cars spun out, allowing Antonelli to move up to fourth place and stretch his championship lead over Russell to 89 points. "I checked in my mirrors and I saw red lights of the back of the cars of the McLarens. So I knew that something happened," Leclerc said. The qualifying session for Sunday's race was delayed due to the rain.

item.title: Jocelyn Bioh on why Broadway is finally ready for ‘School Girls’
item.description: The playwright discusses what has changed since 'School Girls' was first produced, the universality of teenage insecurity and why bringing the play to Broadway feels like coming full circle.
item.dc:creator: Kathryn Lurie
item.content:encoded: Nearly a decade after Jocelyn Bioh wrote “School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play,” the play itself has barely changed. But the world around it has. The comedy about a group of teenage girls at a Ghanaian boarding school premiered off-Broadway in 2017, launching Bioh’s career as a playwright and going on to become a hit at regional theaters across the United States. But despite its success, Bioh was told it might not belong on Broadway. Now “School Girls” has made it there — following the Broadway success of Bioh’s “Jaja’s African Hair Braiding” in 2023 — and she is finding an audience that responds differently to the play’s exploration of body image, the privileging of lighter skin, known as colorism, and the often brutal social dynamics of girlhood. Beneath its rapid-fire jokes and teenage rivalries is a more painful story about who gets to be considered beautiful — and what people are willing to do to fit that ideal. Speaking in New York City, Bioh discusses what has changed since “School Girls” was first produced, the universality of teenage insecurity and why bringing the play to Broadway feels like coming full circle. This conversation has been edited and condensed for clarity. How does it feel to finally bring “School Girls” to Broadway? It feels incredibly humbling. This play changed my life. It was the first play of mine that ever got produced. I can very clearly mark what my life was like before opening night of that show and then after. That audiences and critics all still feel the same way nearly a decade later is a reminder that I was on the right track. It also feels doubly exciting because even though it had so much success regionally and has been all over the country, I was told, “It's a great play, but maybe it's not the right fit for a Broadway stage.” What do you think was meant by that, and what has changed enough for it to be on Broadway now? Broadway shows were very specific then. They didn't have ensembles that looked like the cast of “School Girls.” It was a lot of celebrities, a lot of things that seemed to fit into one specific category or box. The world has shifted. Audiences are different than they were 10 years ago. In a lot of ways, “Jaja's African Hair Braiding” having so much success was a marker that, a Broadway play is just a play that's on Broadway. It doesn't necessarily have to fit a specific category. Is there anything in the play that hits differently than it did when you first wrote it? The conversation around beauty standards and body image has shifted in the last 10 years. Some would say (for the) better, some would say worse, but we're all aware of it in a different way. The play kicks off with Paulina bullying Nana about her size and her eating. You can feel the audience is immediately on Nana's side. Halfway through the play, she has a moment where she really stands up to Paulina, and every night that moment gets applause. You can feel the audience cheering, almost jumping up ready to fight with her. They're taking off their earrings! We did not have that experience off-Broadway. I think we were in a time where we accepted the idea that if you were somebody who was bigger, you should be losing weight; you should be trying to conform. Our ideas of beauty are very different now. Big ships turn slow, but I appreciate that I can feel that in the audience. Did you rewrite much for this production? Very small things, little jokes that I thought would land better. But the play is still largely the same thing I wrote in 2016. If I were sitting down to write this play now, I don't know that I would be as honest or as vulnerable as I was then, particularly in the moments where Paulina is speaking very directly about how colorism has affected her life. I think I would censor myself a little bit now. I never thought the play would get produced, so I was very free and vulnerable in a way. Why? When you're a playwright and your name starts to grow within the community, you start to have an awareness of the responsibility of your words. And I'm okay with having that responsibility because I know I'm doing something really different. I'm really blowing open how people see Black and African people on a theatrical stage. There's an incredible responsibility to that. The play takes place in Ghana, but these girls feel instantly recognizable. Did you know when you were writing it how universal they would be? I understood that there's a real rich universality we have, particularly in school and friendship dynamics. Those things are evergreen and universal. I knew what I was writing was different, (that) the girls and the people I was reflecting were different, but I didn't want to alienate audiences. That's part of why I added the subtitle. What's something we all know and recognize about the teenage experience? Mean girls. Paulina seems to believe that if she can just become Miss Ghana, she can escape the limits of her life. Is her obsession with beauty really an obsession with power and possibility? Probably. Ultimately, I think she really believes this is going to set her up for a successful life in entertainment. The play is set in 1986, and if you became Miss Ghana, Miss World, Miss Universe — any of those things — you could become a star. This is how we have Vanessa Williams or Halle Berry or Kenya Moore, if you're of the “Real Housewives” persuasion. (Another character,) Eloise, is a former Miss Ghana and did leave. She's come back now living a different life, (signifying that) in order to have success, you've got to get out. In order to have power, you have to get out. Maybe Paulina doesn't see the beauty and power that she can build in her own country. That's reflective of so many immigrant, particularly African immigrant, stories: In order to have success, you need to leave. I don't know if the play were set in 2026, (if) that would be the case now. I think the play would be very different. But for Paulina and her circumstances then, that is what she believed. The play deals so directly with colorism. Do you think colorism is in some ways more sensitive to talk about than racism? They're inextricably linked. The play largely talks about and shows the effects of colorism, but then ends with a global lesson on racism. And we've not moved on from it. When we started rehearsals for the play in August, the biggest news story was Lupita Nyong'o playing Helen of Troy in Christopher Nolan's film (“The Odyssey”). (Her casting) did not fit with whomever's standard of beauty (for) the woman whose face launched a thousand ships. Why didn't it fit? Why were there so many suggestions about, “Well, Zendaya's in the movie, why can't she play that part?” That's a very clear conversation about colorism, whether people are using that word or not. When I wrote this play, it was really important for me to have that conversation because it had affected my life so much. Revisiting it now, especially in relation to these conversations that are happening globally, I'm like, well, we've not moved on from it. We can't move on from colorism because nobody's moved on from racism. I can't change people's minds. But if people come to see “School Girls” and their implicit bias can shift just a little bit, then I've done my job. The play is extremely funny until you realize how much pain is sitting underneath the humor. How deliberate is that? I really believe that comedy is just a funny way of being serious. Humor and pain are on two different sides of a truth coin. It's all rooted in truth. Paulina is a girl in the world who's trying to be affirmed and validated that she belongs there, that her beauty is widely accepted even if she knows that it's not. The lengths she goes to get there are what's comical, but it's rooted in something real that we all experience. At the end of the day, I'm a comedic writer and I want people to be entertained. But because I know the responsibility of who I'm introducing and the culture I'm introducing, I think there's a responsibility in also educating people. If I can make that medicine go down with a little bit of sugar, honey, agave, whatever you like, I'm willing to go there.
